<!-- Generated by scripts/build_help.py from Puzzle's own data: don't edit. -->


Model edits go through the same commands the GUI uses, so they appear in the history, can be undone, and wait for approval at the autonomy level set.

<!-- key: mcp:autonomy -->
### autonomy

The autonomy level, budget and what agents have used of it.

<!-- key: mcp:bolt_make_beam -->
### bolt_make_beam

Turn a modelled bolt (ADR 0077) back into a beam bolt: its parts, geometries, materials, contacts, the plates' selections made for them, its pretension feature and mesh sizes removed; its name, type and preload kept. Returns `batch` to pass to submit (one undo); nothing is made here.

Arguments: `bolt`, `component`.

<!-- key: mcp:bolt_make_modelled -->
### bolt_make_modelled

Model bolts as solids drawn from the fastener tables (ADR 0077): each named bolt (`bolt`: a name or a list) becomes a part of its own, the standard bolt by its type's head (hex or socket) and size, placed on its holes' axis, its grade as its material, its head (and nut) on the plates by a frictional contact (the type's head_friction; `bonded_heads` bonds them), its thread into the tapped hole or nut by a threaded contact, its preload on a section across the shank, and finer elements at the fillet and thread; plain washers too when the bolt's `washers` (or its type's) says head, nut or both. Needs a tapped or bolt-and-nut joint. Its loads then come from that section (bolt_results), and the fatigue tool takes the bolt's thread_kf as Kf at its thread. Returns `batch` to pass to submit (one undo); nothing is made here.

Arguments: `bolt`, `bonded_heads`, `component`.

<!-- key: mcp:bolt_results -->
### bolt_results

Each bolt's loads in a study's latest run (ADR 0050), worst first: axial (N, + tension), shear (N), torsion and bending at each end (N m), the stress |N|/As + M/Z (Pa) and its share of the grade's proof and yield strengths.

Arguments: `step`, `study`.

<!-- key: mcp:bolt_sizes -->
### bolt_sizes

Standard bolt sizes (ADR 0050) for bolt types: `standard` iso_coarse, iso_fine (M3-M64), unc (to 4 in) or unf; `contains` filters the names. Each with diameter, pitch, stress area, the bearing diameter joint styles use, the ISO 273 medium clearance hole, and the `head` and `nut` style's bearing diameter and height from the standard part tables (head hex, hex_cap, heavy_hex, structural, socket, button, flat, low_head; nut hex, heavy_hex, thin). All m, m^2.

Arguments: `contains`, `head`, `nut`, `standard`.

<!-- key: mcp:bolt_vdi2230 -->
### bolt_vdi2230

A single-bolt joint by VDI 2230-1:2015 (concentric): bolt and parts' resiliences (head 0.5 d hex / 0.4 d socket, engaged thread 0.5 d, nut 0.4 d or tapped 0.33 d, cone and sleeve), load factor Phi (n by `n`, Table 2), assembly preload FMzul (90 % of Rp0.2 at `mu_thread`), its tightening torque and nut factor K, embedding loss; with `axial_load` (N) the bolt's extra load, equivalent stress and fatigue safety; with `tightening_factor` (alpha_A, Table A8) the least preload and residual clamp load. `size` a bolt_sizes name; `grade` 8.8, 10.9, 12.9 or `rp02` (Pa); `clamp_length`, `shank_length`, `bearing`, `hole`, `outer_diameter`, `rz` in m; moduli in Pa; `head` hex or socket; `tapped` true for a cap screw in a tapped hole. Defaults are listed in `notes`. Nothing is changed.

Arguments: `axial_load`, `bearing`, `clamp_length`, `e_bolt`, `e_nut`, `e_plate`, `grade`, `head`, `hole`, `interfaces`, `mu_head`, `mu_thread`, `n`, `outer_diameter`, `rp02`, `rz`, `shank_length`, `size`, `tapped`, `tightening_factor`.

<!-- key: mcp:bolts_generate -->
### bolts_generate

Propose bolts for a component's holes (ADR 0050). Holes are the parts' cylindrical faces; a bolt joins a stack of holes on one axis in different bodies (of different parts, or several bodies of one part), any number of layers: from the first hole to the last, the ones between in `through`. With a rule (`rule` names it): hole diameters `min_diameter`/`max_diameter` (m), `parts`, an `axis` [x, y, z] (within 5 degrees), lengths between the holes' centres `min_length`/`max_length` (m); or `first` and `second`, two face selections (Part/Selection) whose holes pair up. `bolt_type` is a bolt type's name, else each hole gets the largest type that fits; `names` a pattern with {n}; `group` where they are listed. `ground_unpaired`: a hole with no partner gets a bolt to ground (an anchor, `ground_length` m below it, default 2 d); `same_part`: two holes of one part may be joined; `bearing_faces`: imprint the rings under heads and nuts in the parts' geometry. Returns the proposals, the bolts the rule made before that have lost their holes (`stale`), and `make_bolts`, the batch to pass to submit (face selections, bolts, the rule kept on the component). Nothing is made here.

Arguments: `axis`, `bearing_faces`, `bolt_type`, `component`, `first`, `ground_length`, `ground_unpaired`, `group`, `material`, `max_diameter`, `max_length`, `min_diameter`, `min_length`, `names`, `parts`, `rule`, `same_part`, `second`.

<!-- key: mcp:capabilities -->
### capabilities

What a solver supports: every field of its capability matrix (physics -> step types, features, contacts, axes_features, amplitude_features, time_schemes, material_models, ...). `planned_physics` exists in the solver but isn't written yet; `experimental` isn't verified. check_study gives the real answer for a study.

Arguments: `solver`.

<!-- key: mcp:check_study -->
### check_study

Whether a study can be written for its solver(s); problems if not.

Arguments: `study`.

<!-- key: mcp:contact_check -->
### contact_check

Check a component's contacts before solving (ADR 0056): per contact its setup, what each solver is given (`solver_input`, from the code that writes the input), and its initial state on the mesh: `status` (closed, near, open, far, overhanging), `shares` of the source face's area by status, the largest gap and penetration and the nearest distance (m), and the search distance (m). `warnings` name each contact problem and its fix (overhanging source faces, held or bolted source nodes, faces far apart, a shared outline under Code_Aster friction, bodies held only by sliding contact). `solver`: one solver's view; default the component's studies'. Meshes the component.

Arguments: `component`, `solver`.

<!-- key: mcp:contact_results -->
### contact_results

Each frictionless or frictional contact's results in a study's latest run (ADR 0056): normal and frictional force (N), area in contact (m^2 and share of the source face), largest pressure (Pa), penetration, gap and sliding (m), and the share of the contact area sticking. `step`: a result step, 1-based among those with contact results (default the last). The fields contact_pressure, contact_shear, contact_gap, contact_sliding and contact_status (0 open, 1 sliding, 2 sticking) on the source faces are read with the result_* tools.

Arguments: `step`, `study`.

<!-- key: mcp:contact_thread -->
### contact_thread

Make a contact a thread (ADR 0076): the two smooth coaxial cylinders stay smooth and the contact acts along the flanks, giving each thread's load, the nut's wedge and the engagement's stiffness. `form` iso, un, acme, stub_acme, trapezoidal, buttress, buttress_din, square, npt, bspt or custom (`thread_forms`); `size` a standard size for iso/un (M16, M16x1.5, 1/2-13 UNC), else `major` and `pitch` as quantities ({"value": 20, "unit": "mm"}); custom needs `flank_angles` [load, other] degrees. `starts`, `hand` right/left, `bearing` auto (the pull decides the side)/load/other, `compliance` teeth/rigid or N/m^3, `clearance` (backlash), `engaged_length`, `cs` a coordinate system's name whose z is the axis. `type` changes the contact's type: bonded (ties the bearing flank), no_separation (both flanks), frictionless (unilateral: nonlinear). `remove` clears the thread. Returns the resolved numbers (m), notes, and `command`: pass it to submit. Nothing is changed here.

Arguments: `bearing`, `clearance`, `compliance`, `component`, `contact`, `cs`, `engaged_length`, `flank_angles`, `form`, `hand`, `major`, `pitch`, `remove`, `size`, `starts`, `type`.

<!-- key: mcp:contacts_find -->
### contacts_find

Find where the parts of a component touch (ADR 0039), and the bodies of a part with several (an imported STEP assembly is often one part): one proposal per pair of parts or bodies with the faces on each side, the gap (m) and the overlap (m^2); `source_body`/`target_body` name the bodies (null between whole parts). Bodies of one part share their nodes where they touch (Share faces): a bonded contact between them records that, a frictionless or frictional one parts them. `tolerance` is the largest gap in m (default 0.5 % of the model's size), `angle` how far from face to face, in degrees. `make_bonded` is the batch that makes every proposal as a bonded contact (face selections first); change a contact's type or drop proposals, then pass the list to submit. Nothing is made here. `thread`, when set, says the two sides are coaxial cylinders of near-equal radius (a tapped hole or a screw in a nut?) with a likely ISO size: make the contact, then `contact_thread` (ADR 0076).

Arguments: `angle`, `component`, `tolerance`.

<!-- key: mcp:derived_result -->
### derived_result

A derived result (combination or equation, ADR 0025): what it reads, the results it gives (field names for result_stats etc., which take its name in place of a study), warnings, and for equations the names an expression may use.

Arguments: `name`.

<!-- key: mcp:element_choose -->
### element_choose

Choose the element a body is written with (ADR 0082 step 3): `selection` a body selection ('Part/Body') or part, `formulation` in neutral words (incompatible_modes: linear bricks bending without locking, CalculiX C3D8I; mixed_up: nearly incompressible, Code_Aster 3D_INCO_UPG; euler_bernoulli: slender beams, Code_Aster POU_D_E; lumped: heat capacity without undershoot, Code_Aster 3D_DIAG; full, timoshenko, thin_shell: the defaults), `solver_types` an expert's own {solver: type}. `formulation` 'none' removes the body's choice. Each solver maps it from the element library (elements_list) or refuses it, naming what it has. One edit; at 'propose' a proposal.

Arguments: `component`, `formulation`, `rationale`, `selection`, `solver_types`.

<!-- key: mcp:elements_list -->
### elements_list

The element library (ADR 0082): every solver's elements with their family, cells, formulation (full or reduced integration, incompatible modes, mixed u-p, thick or thin shell, Euler-Bernoulli or Timoshenko...), the studies they support, what each is for and not for, whether Puzzle writes it yet, and the manual's section. Filter by `solver`, `family` (solid_3d, solid_2d, shell, beam, truss, discrete, thermal, electromagnetic, fluid), `study` (static, modal, buckling, transient, harmonic, contact, plasticity, large_deflection, heat, electrostatics, magnetics, flow) or `written`. element_choose picks one for a body.

Arguments: `family`, `solver`, `study`, `written`.

<!-- key: mcp:equation_names -->
### equation_names

The names an equation over a study's latest run may use (von_mises, deformation_y, stress_xx, ...), and the project parameters.

Arguments: `study`.

<!-- key: mcp:error_estimate -->
### error_estimate

Error estimate (ADR 0066 phase 2) of a study's newest run (or a sweep point's, `point` as its title), from the stored field: displacement gives the Zienkiewicz–Zhu energy-norm error, temperature the same on the heat flux, `field` any nodal field's gradient jumps (relative only). Returns the relative error, how many elements are too big for `target` (0.02 = 2 %), the hot spots (element, error, centre in m, selections touched) and notes. Solves nothing.

Arguments: `field`, `point`, `study`, `target`.

<!-- key: mcp:explicit_estimate -->
### explicit_estimate

An explicit dynamics study's time step and cost before it runs (ADR 0085): meshes its component and gives the stable time step (s, the element setting it and where), the cycles to the step's end time at its time-step scale, the model's mass, and when the run would pass 1e7 cycles the mass scaling time step for about 1e6 with the mass it would add (kg and share), plus warnings.

Arguments: `study`.

<!-- key: mcp:export -->
### export

Write a study's latest results for other software (ADR 0043). format: abaqus_displacement, abaqus_inp, cgns, deformed_step, deformed_stl, ensight, exodus, gltf, lorentz_cloud, morphed_step, nastran, paraview, point_cloud, tecplot, unv, vtkhdf, wall_cloud. Which to choose, and each one's options: skill_read('exports'). path is inside the project folder (e.g. exports/shape). axes (a coordinate system's name, ADR 0049): vectors and tensors in its axes. Returns the files written.

Arguments: `axes`, `compensate`, `format`, `path`, `quantity`, `scale`, `selection`, `step`, `study`.

<!-- key: mcp:fastener_tables -->
### fastener_tables

Standard fastener tables (ADR 0050): screws, nuts and washers as ISO, DIN, ASME and ASTM tabulate them (from Lacewing Lab's tables). No `table`: each table's id, title, standard, kind and sizes. With `table` (e.g. iso.hexBolt, asme.hexNut, iso.washerNormal): its reference, notes, columns and rows (one `size` as the table names it: M10, 1/2, #10); lengths in m, threads per inch as counts.

Arguments: `size`, `table`.

<!-- key: mcp:field_check -->
### field_check

An imported field's verification report (ADR 0044): points, each column's range and mean (SI), and with `on` (a component, or Component/Part/Selection) the share of it within `tolerance_mm` of a data point, the farthest distance, points off the model, and warnings (sparse data, uncovered areas, a length unit that looks wrong). Meshes the component when `on` is given.

Arguments: `field`, `on`, `tolerance_mm`.

<!-- key: mcp:field_import -->
### field_import

Read a field file (ADR 0044: x, y, z and values: CSV/TXT/DAT, VTU, a Fluent profile .prof, Exodus II .exo/.e, EnSight Gold .case, or an OpenFOAM case folder) that is inside the project folder (`file`, relative to it) and say how it would be read: format, columns with their roles (x, y, z, value, time, frequency, ignore) and units, the points' length unit, and for multi-step sources their `steps` (time, index) and `regions` (blocks, parts, patches, profiles). `region` reads one of those, `index` one step (default the last). Varying in time: `files` (more files, one per time, same layout) with `times` (s, one per file, `file`'s first), or `every_step` (every step of the source, at its own times or at `times`); a CSV time column is a column with role time. Varying with frequency (for harmonic steps only): `frequencies` (Hz) in place of `times`, or a CSV column with role frequency. Returns `create`, the command that adds it as an imported field: change its `columns`, `length_unit`, or `placement` (translation m, rotation degrees about x, y, z, about m, axes a coordinate system's id) if the guess is wrong, then pass it to `submit`. Check it with `field_check` first.

Arguments: `every_step`, `file`, `files`, `frequencies`, `index`, `name`, `region`, `times`.

<!-- key: mcp:frame_geometry -->
### frame_geometry

A frame's geometry (ADR 0079): line members between named nodes, or a DXF's LINE/LWPOLYLINE/POLYLINE entities (layers become member groups). `nodes` {name: [x, y, z]} in metres, `members` [[name, i, j], or [name, i, j, group]]; or `dxf` (a file in the project), `layer`, `scale` (m per drawing unit; default from $INSUNITS, mm when unset). Gives edge selections per member and group and point selections per node. Returns `command` (a create) to pass to submit; nothing is made here. Then a component with the geometry as a part, a beam section on it (or per group), a material, supports and loads at nodes (skill `frames`).

Arguments: `dxf`, `layer`, `members`, `name`, `nodes`, `scale`.

<!-- key: mcp:frame_grid -->
### frame_grid

A frame's geometry from a grid (ADR 0079 step 6), as SAP2000's and RISA's templates: `bays_x` and `bays_y` (widths in m; bays_y empty for a plane frame in x-z), `stories` (heights in m), `columns`, `beams`, `bracing` none, x or chevron, `braced_bays` ends (the first and last bay of each outside frame line) or all. Nodes are named by column line, row and level (A1-0 at the base, levels up from 0); members are grouped Columns, Beams X, Beams Y, Braces. Returns `command` (a create) for submit, as frame_geometry does, and the counts.

Arguments: `bays_x`, `bays_y`, `beams`, `braced_bays`, `bracing`, `columns`, `name`, `stories`.

<!-- key: mcp:frame_members -->
### frame_members

A frame component's members (ADR 0079): each member's ends, length (m), group and section (or none), the nodes, member end releases and rigid offsets, and the supports and loads. Frames solve on PyNite (releases, offsets, line loads, node springs, self weight) and on CalculiX and Code_Aster beams (no releases yet).

Arguments: `component`.

<!-- key: mcp:geometry_check -->
### geometry_check

Check a geometry for what would trouble meshing or solving: gaps, surfaces that are not solids, short edges, slivers, overlapping or unshared bodies.

Arguments: `geometry`.

<!-- key: mcp:geometry_measure -->
### geometry_measure

Exact measurements of named geometry (ADR 0042), from the CAD shape: picks are [{entity: body|face|edge|vertex, name, part?}]. With `component`, picks name a part each and are measured where the parts are placed. One pick: length, area, volume, radius, centroid, normal or axis; two: minimum distance (and where), centre distance with dx, dy, dz, angle (degrees); more: totals. SI units.

Arguments: `component`, `geometry`, `picks`.

<!-- key: mcp:get_object -->
### get_object

One object's full data (JSON), by name or id.

Arguments: `name`.

<!-- key: mcp:help -->
### help

Puzzle's manual (ADR 0083), the pages people read in the Help window: no `topic` gives the contents; a page name ('guides/meshing', 'reference/settings') or a help key ('feature:pressure', 'setting:calculix:solver', 'operator:reduce', 'problem:unconstrained') gives that page, from the entry the key names; any other words search it. Cite pages by their title when you explain from them.

Arguments: `topic`.

<!-- key: mcp:history -->
### history

Recent history entries, newest first.

Arguments: `limit`.

<!-- key: mcp:host_check -->
### host_check

Reach a remote host over SSH and say what it has: reachable or why not, its cores, which solvers run there, whether its scheduler answers.

Arguments: `name`.

<!-- key: mcp:hosts_list -->
### hosts_list

The user's remote hosts (their hosts.toml): name, address, how solvers run there, scheduler, cores. A study runs on one when its `remote` names it, or run_study has `host`. Hosts are the user's: agents list and check them, never add them.

<!-- key: mcp:job_cancel -->
### job_cancel

Stop a pending job (its id, or its study's name: all its jobs). It stays listed until resumed or dismissed by the user. Agents cancel only where the autonomy level lets them act.

Arguments: `job`.

<!-- key: mcp:job_resume -->
### job_resume

Pick up a pending job (its id, or its study's name): the same run attached to the job, its results stored as from any run. A run, so the autonomy level decides: refused at advise, a proposal at propose.

Arguments: `job`.

<!-- key: mcp:jobs_list -->
### jobs_list

The project's solves that are with a job runner and not home yet (ADR 0067): each job's id, study, solver, where (this computer or a host), state in words (Queued, Running, Finished, Failed, Cancelled, ...), elapsed seconds and the log's last line. A finished one waits for job_resume to bring its results home. `live` asks remote hosts too (SSH: slow).

Arguments: `live`.

<!-- key: mcp:knowledge -->
### knowledge

Search Puzzle's domain pack: the skills, curated solver notes (what Puzzle learned about each solver), each solver's capabilities, Code_Aster's French messages in English, and the ADRs. Returns passages with a citation (source § heading) and, for manual summaries, a link. Cite what you use.

Arguments: `limit`, `query`.

<!-- key: mcp:link -->
### link

Wire one object into another (ADR 0071 decision 8), as drawing a wire in the schematic does: a material onto a component (which part), a mesh recipe onto a component, a component into a study, a coordinate system or amplitude onto a component's load, a study onto a result tool or derived result, a construction plane onto a result tool, a bolt type onto a bolt; with `feature` (a component's load or support as the schematic names it, 'Pressure on Bracket/Inner'), onto that load: its coordinate system, amplitude, or (a geometry) the selection it acts on. Without `which`, lists what the wire could mean (`choices`, each with its index and label) and applies it when there is exactly one; with `which` (an index or a label), applies that one. A wire that fits nowhere says what the target takes. One undoable command.

Arguments: `feature`, `rationale`, `source`, `target`, `which`.

<!-- key: mcp:load_combinations -->
### load_combinations

A frame study's load combinations (ADR 0079 step 2; PyNite solves them, one result step each, named): `method` 'LRFD' or 'ASD' generates ASCE 7-16's (2.3.1, 2.4.1) from the load cases its component's loads use (each load's `case`: D, L, Lr, S, R, W, E; wind and seismic both ways); or `combinations` = [{name, factors: {case: factor}}] sets your own; neither lists the cases and the current ones. Second order (P-Delta) and AISC's Direct Analysis Method are the solve step's settings second_order and direct_analysis (notional_directions, default 'x,y'). One edit; at 'propose' a proposal.

Arguments: `combinations`, `method`, `rationale`, `study`.

<!-- key: mcp:magnetic_check -->
### magnetic_check

A magnetic study's skin-depth check (ADR 0047): each conductor's skin depth δ at the study's highest frequency, the element size its mesh recipe asks for, whether that is coarser than δ/2, and the refine-near controls to append to the recipe's `controls` (one Edit) when it is.

Arguments: `study`.

<!-- key: mcp:material_check -->
### material_check

What a material can be used for (ADR 0020): for each solver and analysis, the properties it lacks and the material models that solver would refuse. `material` is a project material's name, or a library key.

Arguments: `material`.

<!-- key: mcp:materials_export -->
### materials_export

The user's material library as one file to share, written inside the project folder (e.g. exports/materials.json). scope: yours (made in the builder), user (imported and yours) or all (with Puzzle's generics). Agents never import one: the user does, Materials -> Import material library... (ADR 0020).

Arguments: `path`, `scope`.

<!-- key: mcp:materials_library -->
### materials_library

Materials in the library whose name or group contains `text`.

Arguments: `text`.

<!-- key: mcp:member_checks -->
### member_checks

Frame members checked by their material's code (ADR 0079 steps 3 and 5): carbon steel by AISC 360-16, stainless by AISC 370-21, aluminium by the Aluminum Design Manual 2015, from a study's latest run: per member its section, code, method (LRFD or ASD, from member_design), the governing check over the steps (check, limit state, clause, demand, available strength, ratio, station along the member in m, the combination), passes, and each step's checks: tension (D2), compression (E3, E4, E7), flexure about x per unbraced segment with its C_b and about y (F2-F11), shear along each axis (G2-G6), HSS torsion (H3), combined forces (H1-1), deflection when a limit is set. Members sorted worst first; `not_checked` says why (channels, angles and tees not built yet). Forces in N and N·m. `member` one of them; `step` 1-based among the static steps; `summary` drops the per-step lists.

Arguments: `member`, `step`, `study`, `summary`.

<!-- key: mcp:member_design -->
### member_design

How a frame's members are checked (ADR 0079 step 3): sets or replaces the entry for `selection` (Part/Member, Part/Group, the part, or '' for every member; the most specific wins). `method` LRFD or ASD; lengths as quantities (e.g. '10 ft'): `unbraced_length` L_b for lateral-torsional buckling (and the default for y and z), `length_x`/`length_y`/`length_z` the buckling lengths, unset the member's own; `k_x`, `k_y`, `k_z` effective length factors (1 under Direct Analysis); `cb` overrides the computed C_b; `net_area_ratio` A_e/A_g for tensile rupture; `deflection_limit` 360 for L/360. `remove` drops the entry. The code follows the material: carbon and low-alloy steel by AISC 360-16, stainless by AISC 370-21, aluminium by the Aluminum Design Manual 2015. Never changes a solve. One edit; at 'propose' a proposal.

Arguments: `cb`, `component`, `deflection_limit`, `k_x`, `k_y`, `k_z`, `length_x`, `length_y`, `length_z`, `method`, `net_area_ratio`, `rationale`, `remove`, `selection`, `unbraced_length`.

<!-- key: mcp:mesh_adapt -->
### mesh_adapt

Adaptive refinement (ADR 0066 phase 3): solve, estimate the error, mesh again with each element sized for `target` (0.02 = 2 %), pass after pass, until the energy-norm error (or, with the study's adapt.criterion 'quantity', its quantities' change) is at the target or `passes` ran. Settings default to the study's `adapt`. `method` 'anisotropic' remeshes with MMG along the field's Hessian (thin layers: heat, flow); 'isotropic' with the recipe's mesher. Each pass is a stored run, reused next time. `solve` false (the default) only reads the passes run; solving is a run: refused at advise, a proposal at propose, each pass counted against the budget at act_in_budget.

Arguments: `method`, `passes`, `solve`, `study`, `target`.

<!-- key: mcp:mesh_convergence -->
### mesh_convergence

Mesh convergence (ADR 0066): the study (or a mesh study, by name) on `levels` meshes, each one's sizes divided by `ratio`, its quantities judged by Roache's grid convergence index: observed order, extrapolated value, GCI against `target` (0.02 = 2 %). `solve` false (the default) only reads the meshes already run; solving is a run: refused at advise, a proposal at propose, each level counted against the budget at act_in_budget. Each level is a stored run, reused next time.

Arguments: `levels`, `ratio`, `solve`, `study`, `target`.

<!-- key: mcp:mesh_quality -->
### mesh_quality

Mesh a component with its recipe and report the mesh (ADR 0019): node and element counts, each quality measure's min, mean and histogram (shape and scaled Jacobian 0..1, 1 ideal; edge aspect ratio from 1), the worst-shaped elements with their centres (m), and the mesher's warnings. A mesh that fails says why (conflicting sizes, an unknown option, a quality floor missed).

Arguments: `component`.

<!-- key: mcp:mesh_shootout -->
### mesh_shootout

Run a study on its mesh recipe meshed by Gmsh and by Netgen and compare (ADR 0019): each quantity's peak (or a global value), or 'eigenfrequencies', as a relative difference against `tolerance`. Slow: it solves the study twice. A run: the autonomy level decides (a proposal at propose) and both solves count against the budget.

Arguments: `quantities`, `study`, `tolerance`.

<!-- key: mcp:model_values -->
### model_values

What a Model value can read from an object (ADR 0071 step 3): every value it holds, each with its label (pass it as the operator's `property`), path, quantity kind and whether it's a table against temperature. Without `object`, the objects that hold readable values.

Arguments: `object`.

<!-- key: mcp:next_steps -->
### next_steps

What the project needs next (ADR 0040, the Advisor): the workflow's steps for a component and study (the first of each if not named) as done, needed or optional, each with its reason, and `next`, the first needed one. The same advice the GUI's Advisor shows.

Arguments: `component`, `study`.

<!-- key: mcp:operator_add -->
### operator_add

Add an operator (ADR 0062): `type` reduce, filter, check, panel, plot, export (after solving) or number, slider, series, range, expression, table, list, pairs (data, before solving: Numbers, Sliders and Expressions then act as parameters by their name); `inputs` by port, each {source: a study, derived result, result tool, parameter set or operator by name, port: its output} or {value: '200 MPa'}; a wire from a study (or its result tool) may say which run it reads: point (a sweep point, mesh level or adaptive pass by its title, 'load = 300 N'), solver (a shoot-out's) or run (a stored run by its name), else the study's run for its model now; a swept study needs its point; `settings` its own fields (quantity, selection, reduction, step, keep, compare, against, file, format, low, high, increment, expression, text, operation, column, combination). A study's ports: result, or a field (stress). Read the skill schematic-operators first, and operator_help for what a type does and its ports. One undoable command; returns its value.

Arguments: `inputs`, `name`, `rationale`, `settings`, `type`.

<!-- key: mcp:operator_export -->
### operator_export

Write an Export or Report operator's file now (Export now): an export's value as CSV, Parquet, Excel, a result format or a PNG; a report's checks, numbers, curves and tables as one HTML file. Always inside the project folder. Returns the files written, relative to the project.

Arguments: `name`.

<!-- key: mcp:operator_help -->
### operator_help

What operators do (ADR 0071), before using one: with no arguments every operator kind (its type for operator_add, its name, group and purpose); with `type` (or an operator's name as shown) its full card: purpose, an example, each input (what it takes, needed or not, whether a value can be typed) and output; with `search`, the kinds whose name, purpose or other names match (e.g. 'maximum', 'divide', 'pivot').

Arguments: `search`, `type`.

<!-- key: mcp:operator_value -->
### operator_value

An operator's value (ADR 0062): its outputs in SI (a number with its unit and where a maximum is, a verdict with its margin, a table's rows), what the schematic node shows, and how it is wired. `runs`: the stored runs it read, each with `stale` (true: not the study's run for its model now; `stale` on the whole says any was, and a stale verdict is no pass). `run_choices`: per input wired from a study, the runs it may read (give one to operator_add or an edit as `point`, `solver` or `run`). `needs_runs`: the studies it reads, through every operator upstream, that aren't up to date: run_study each (the GUI's Evaluate up to here). An `error` with code operator_failed is that operator's own (a formula too large, a text where a number goes) or an input's. Without a name: every operator.

Arguments: `name`.

<!-- key: mcp:optimisation_apply -->
### optimisation_apply

Put an optimisation's best feasible point (or point `index`) into the model's parameters (ADR 0063): one batch, so one undo; a version is saved first. At 'propose' it becomes a proposal for the user to accept.

Arguments: `index`, `name`, `rationale`.

<!-- key: mcp:optimisation_points -->
### optimisation_points

An optimisation's points (ADR 0063), from the stored runs, solving nothing: each point's variables (SI and as labelled), its runs, objective, constraints, feasible or why not; the best feasible point, the suggestion to apply it, each variable's sensitivities (correlation with each output), how an optimiser `ended`, the `pareto` front's point indexes, a response surface's `surface_fit` (leave-one-out error per output, a share of its range), and robust design's `robust` (the design chosen; each output's mean, sd and ±3σ range over the scatter, SI; each constraint's probability of holding; the surface's miss at each checked point).

Arguments: `name`.

<!-- key: mcp:optimisation_run -->
### optimisation_run

Run an optimisation's points (ADR 0063). A run, as run_study is: refused at advise, a proposal at propose, and at act_in_budget each point solved counts against the budget, which stops it when spent. Each point is a stored run, a point run before is reused, so a stopped optimiser resumes on its path; `budget` solves at most that many new points this time. Returns the points as optimisation_points.

Arguments: `budget`, `name`.

<!-- key: mcp:outline -->
### outline

The model tree as compact text, with any problems.

Arguments: `ids`.

<!-- key: mcp:pardiso_build -->
### pardiso_build

Start building CalculiX with Intel MKL's PARDISO on this computer, in the background (minutes; contact and large solves then factor 2-4x faster with the same answers). Returns at once; follow it with solvers_list. Only when the user asks: the GUI already builds it once by itself.

<!-- key: mcp:parts_split -->
### parts_split

Split a part holding several bodies (an imported STEP assembly) into one part per body (ADR 0039): each body a geometry of its own (the file imported, then that body kept), named by the body's selection; every reference follows its body (materials, loads, supports, contacts, bolts, mesh sizes, result tools), and one on a selection spanning bodies is repeated per part where it can be (materials, features, sections) or reported in `notes`. `bond` (default true) adds bonded contacts where the bodies touch, as the part's Share faces joined them. Returns the plan; `batch` is the list to pass to submit (one undo). Nothing is made here.

Arguments: `bond`, `component`, `part`.

<!-- key: mcp:preview -->
### preview

What commands would change, and the problems left, without applying.

Arguments: `commands`.

<!-- key: mcp:probe_history -->
### probe_history

A kept probe at every step of its source's current run (ADR 0038): [{step: time, increment or frequency, value (SI)}], for load-deflection curves and transients.

Arguments: `name`.

<!-- key: mcp:probe_path -->
### probe_path

A path result tool's series (ADR 0042): distance along the path (m) and the value there (SI; null outside the model).

Arguments: `name`.

<!-- key: mcp:probes -->
### probes

Every result tool (ADR 0032, 0042) read for its source's current run: point probes (value, point), results over a selection (max, min, mean or integral), reactions (force and moment components, about which point) and paths (largest value and where; the full series with probe_path). SI units.

<!-- key: mcp:problems -->
### problems

Consistency problems of the project, each with a code.

<!-- key: mcp:project_archive -->
### project_archive

The project as one .puzzle archive to share (ADR 0061), written inside the project folder (e.g. exports/model.puzzle). results: none, latest (per study) or all; versions and history true or false. Returns its size by part.

Arguments: `history`, `path`, `results`, `versions`.

<!-- key: mcp:proposals -->
### proposals

Open proposals and their previews.

<!-- key: mcp:propose -->
### propose

Ask the user to review commands before they apply, whatever the level. Use only when you want their review; changes they asked for go through submit.

Arguments: `commands`, `rationale`.

<!-- key: mcp:recipe_insert -->
### recipe_insert

Put a recipe or cluster into the project (ADR 0064): `key` from recipes, `bindings` each port name to a source {"source": id, "port": "result"} (a study's result, a table operator's out). One batch, one undo; at 'propose' a proposal.

Arguments: `bindings`, `key`, `rationale`.

<!-- key: mcp:recipes -->
### recipes

The recipes (ready-wired operator chains: worst nodes, peak per part, solver difference, stress margin, reactions in kN, mass from geometry) and the user's saved clusters (ADR 0064): key, name, help and input ports.

<!-- key: mcp:render -->
### render

A picture of a study's latest result (PNG).

Arguments: `field`, `mode`, `scalar`, `step`, `study`.

<!-- key: mcp:result_history -->
### result_history

A field summed (reduce='total') or averaged ('mean') over a selection at every increment or time: load-deflection curves, transients.

Arguments: `field`, `reduce`, `selection`, `study`.

<!-- key: mcp:result_integral -->
### result_integral

Integral and mean of a nodal field over a body or face selection.

Arguments: `component`, `field`, `selection`, `step`, `study`.

<!-- key: mcp:result_stats -->
### result_stats

Min, max, mean of a field and where the extremes are; optionally on a selection or for one component (default: magnitude, von Mises).

Arguments: `component`, `field`, `selection`, `step`, `study`.

<!-- key: mcp:result_summary -->
### result_summary

Every step and field of a study's latest run, in a few numbers.

Arguments: `study`.

<!-- key: mcp:result_total -->
### result_total

Sum of a nodal field over a selection, e.g. the reaction force on a support or contact face (field reaction_force).

Arguments: `field`, `selection`, `step`, `study`.

<!-- key: mcp:result_value_at -->
### result_value_at

A field at a point (metres); a null coordinate averages along it.

Arguments: `field`, `step`, `study`, `x`, `y`, `z`.

<!-- key: mcp:run_log -->
### run_log

A solve's own logs, read whole from its run folder (solver.log, Code_Aster's .mess, CalculiX's .sta/.cvg, OpenFOAM's log.*): `problems` the error and warning lines by each solver's markers, `pattern` lines matching a regular expression (any case), with `context` lines around; else each file's last `tail` lines. `study` reads its newest attempt (failed or stopped too), `run` a stored run. Use run_progress first for a summary; this is for the solver's words.

Arguments: `context`, `limit`, `pattern`, `problems`, `run`, `study`, `tail`.

<!-- key: mcp:run_progress -->
### run_progress

How a study's last solve went or is going (ADR 0054): steps, increments, cut-backs, iterations, last residuals against their criteria, equations, memory, tracked probes' last values, the solver's warnings and errors in English, and diagnoses (what a failure means and what to try). Reads the newest attempt, so a failed, stopped or running solve is included; `run` picks a stored run instead.

Arguments: `run`, `study`.

<!-- key: mcp:runs -->
### runs

Stored runs: study, solver, when, how long.

<!-- key: mcp:schema -->
### schema

JSON schema: "commands", or an object kind such as "component".

Arguments: `which`.

<!-- key: mcp:schematic -->
### schematic

The project schematic (ADR 0058): every file, resource, component, study and result as a node (column, state and its reason, ports), and the wires between them: `data` wires carry values (transfers, imported fields, runs into derived results; labelled with what flows), `use` wires say what is built from what (geometry into components, components into studies). Give `node` (a name) to get what it is built from (`upstream`) and what would go out of date if it changed (`downstream`). Use it to explain how a project fits together.

Arguments: `node`.

<!-- key: mcp:sections_find -->
### sections_find

Standard structural sections (ADR 0055): `standard` aisc or en; with no `family`, the families; with one, its designations (filtered by `contains`), each with depth and width (m), A (m^2), I strong and weak (m^4), J (m^4) and mass (kg/m).

Arguments: `contains`, `family`, `standard`.

<!-- key: mcp:seismic_design -->
### seismic_design

A frame study's ASCE 7-16 seismic parameters (ADR 0079 step 4): sds, sd1 (g; S_DS and S_D1 from 11.4.4), s1 (g, for 12.8-6), tl (s), r and cd (Table 12.2-1), ie (1.0, 1.25, 1.5), risk_category I-IV, structure for T_a (Table 12.8-2: steel_moment_frame, concrete_moment_frame, steel_eccentrically_braced, steel_buckling_restrained, other), drift_structure for Table 12.12-1 (low_rise_with_partitions, masonry_cantilever_shear_wall, other_masonry_shear_wall, other), period (s) to override the computed one, mass_cases {case: factor} in the seismic weight beyond the members' own (default D at 1), scale_to_elf (1.0 in 7-16), damping (0.05). `clear` removes them. One edit; at 'propose' a proposal. Then seismic_elf writes ELF story forces, or a modal step with response_spectrum true runs modal response spectrum analysis.

Arguments: `cd`, `clear`, `damping`, `drift_structure`, `ie`, `mass_cases`, `period`, `r`, `rationale`, `risk_category`, `s1`, `scale_to_elf`, `sd1`, `sds`, `structure`, `study`, `tl`.

<!-- key: mcp:seismic_elf -->
### seismic_elf

ASCE 7-16's equivalent lateral force procedure on a frame study (12.8): C_s (12.8-2 to 12.8-6, which governed), the period used (computed or `period`, capped at C_u T_a; T_a from Table 12.8-2 without either), W from the members' density and the seismic design's mass_cases, V = C_s W, k, and each level's height, weight, C_vx, F_x and story shear. Writes the forces as loads on the levels' nodes (case Ex or Ey by `direction`, replacing earlier ELF loads that way) unless `write` is false. One edit; at 'propose' a proposal.

Arguments: `direction`, `period`, `rationale`, `study`, `write`.

<!-- key: mcp:seismic_report -->
### seismic_report

A frame study's seismic numbers (ADR 0079 step 4): ELF in x and y (with the modal period where the latest run has modes), each mode's frequency, period, participation factor, effective mass and mass fraction, the summed mass participation (12.9.1.1 wants 90 % each way), each response spectrum's modal base shear V_t, the ELF V, the force scale (12.9.1.4.1) and drift scale, and story drifts (12.8.6: C_d δ / I_e at each level's centre of mass, against Table 12.12-1's Δ_a, ratio ≤ 1 passes) of the spectrum steps or of combinations named Ex or Ey.

Arguments: `study`.

<!-- key: mcp:selections_check -->
### selections_check

How a geometry's selections resolve after edits or a replaced file: each member kept, re-found (by where it was), by rule, or detached with ranked candidates. `accept_all` is an edit command taking every proposal (and a rule where one fits); review it, then pass it to submit.

Arguments: `geometry`.

<!-- key: mcp:sketch_check -->
### sketch_check

Solve a sketch (an extrude or revolve profile {"sketch": {...}}; format in puzzle.geometry.sketch) with the project's parameters: whether it solves, the degrees of freedom left, the conflicting constraints (1-based) and the solved point positions in m. Check a sketch here before submitting it.

Arguments: `sketch`.

<!-- key: mcp:skill_read -->
### skill_read

One skill's how-to: the steps, the tools and their arguments, units and the usual mistakes, for a task in its area.

Arguments: `name`.

<!-- key: mcp:skills_list -->
### skills_list

The skills: one line each, saying when to read it (`skill_read`).

<!-- key: mcp:solver_settings -->
### solver_settings

A study's solver settings (ADR 0023): the shared ones (on each solve step's settings: linear_solver, tolerance, max_iterations, output_every) and each of its solvers' own (Study.solver_settings[solver]), with labels, the solver's own name, choices, defaults and current values, and how that solver's expert pass-through (Study.expert_settings[solver]) is written. Change them with solver_settings_set.

Arguments: `study`.

<!-- key: mcp:solver_settings_set -->
### solver_settings_set

Change a study's solver settings (ADR 0023) in one edit, one undo: `shared` = {key: value} on every solve step it applies to (linear_solver, tolerance, max_iterations, output_every; load stepping: increments, initial_increment, min_increment, fixed_increments); `solvers` = {solver: {key: value}} for each solver's own (convergence: CalculiX cutbacks, cutback_factor, increase_factor; Code_Aster line_search, prediction, matrix, cutback_parts, cutback_levels, absolute_tolerance; Elmer relaxation, newton_after_iterations); `expert` = {solver: {path: value}} replacing that solver's pass-through. A value of null removes a setting. Keys, choices and units: solver_settings. At 'propose' a proposal.

Arguments: `expert`, `rationale`, `shared`, `solvers`, `study`.

<!-- key: mcp:solvers_list -->
### solvers_list

The solvers on this computer and how a solve runs each now: native (its program), in a container (its image) or missing (why); CalculiX's note says PARDISO or SPOOLES, and `pardiso` the state of CalculiX with PARDISO built here (built, building, failed with the reason, ready, unavailable).

<!-- key: mcp:submit -->
### submit

Make a change: one command, or a list of model edits applied together (all or none, undone as one). See schema('commands'). The autonomy level decides whether it is refused, proposed or applied.

Arguments: `command`, `rationale`.

<!-- key: mcp:symmetry_plane -->
### symmetry_plane

Put a symmetry or antisymmetry plane on a component (ADR 0081): `selection` a flat face (a straight edge in 2D), 'Part/Name'; `kind` 'symmetry' (nothing moves through it; on every physics that has one: solid, heat and electrostatic symmetry, fluid symmetry, magnetic symmetry) or 'antisymmetry' (solid mechanics: nothing moves along it). One edit, one undo; at 'propose' a proposal. A 2D or axisymmetric model is the component's `dimension` (an edit).

Arguments: `component`, `kind`, `rationale`, `selection`.

<!-- key: mcp:symmetry_repeat -->
### symmetry_repeat

Make a component one sector or slice of a repeating whole (ADR 0081): `kind` 'cyclic' (the `target` face is the `source` face turned 360/`sectors` degrees about `axis` through `origin`, right-handed; static, transient and heat studies on CalculiX, solid mechanics on Code_Aster) or 'periodic' (the target is the source moved by `translation`, metres). Selections 'Part/Name'; each node on the target moves as its twin on the source. Loads are the sector's own. `kind` 'none' removes both. One edit; at 'propose' a proposal.

Arguments: `axis`, `component`, `kind`, `origin`, `rationale`, `sectors`, `source`, `target`, `translation`.

<!-- key: mcp:thread_forms -->
### thread_forms

Thread forms (ADR 0076) for `contact_thread`: each form's key, name, standard, flank angles (load, other; degrees from the radial plane), taper (diameter per length) and how its size is given; with `form` iso or un, its standard sizes by name (M16, M16x1.5, 1/2-13 UNC).

Arguments: `form`.

<!-- key: mcp:thread_results -->
### thread_results

Threaded contacts' results in a study's latest run (ADR 0076): per thread contact the axial load (N), each engaged thread's axial load and share (the first engaged, at the mouth, first), the wedge (total radial force, N: the nut's opening) and the peak flank pressure (Pa). `contact` one of them; `step` 1-based among the steps with thread results (default the last). The nodal fields thread_force (normal, axial, radial) and thread_pressure are read with result_*.

Arguments: `contact`, `step`, `study`.

<!-- key: mcp:undo -->
### undo

Undo your own latest change, or history entry `seq`.

Arguments: `seq`.

<!-- key: mcp:unlink -->
### unlink

Remove a reference between two objects (ADR 0071 decision 8), as removing a wire in the schematic does. Without `which`, lists what joins them; with `which` (an index or label), clears it. A reference an object can't be without (a study's component) is refused: link another to replace it.

Arguments: `feature`, `rationale`, `source`, `target`, `which`.

<!-- key: mcp:version_restore -->
### version_restore

Make the project a version's again: its number, or 'good' for the latest known good. The state replaced is kept as a version and undo takes the restore back. Agents restore only where the autonomy level lets them act.

Arguments: `version`.

<!-- key: mcp:version_save -->
### version_save

Save a version of the project as it is now (before a risky batch of changes, say), with a label; `good` marks it known good.

Arguments: `good`, `label`, `note`.

<!-- key: mcp:versions_list -->
### versions_list

The project's versions, newest first: number, time, by, what, known good, and each one's summary (studies and their state, what changed). Filter by who (by: you, puzzle, agent), types (user, first, opened, before_run, edits, before_restore, copied), since/until (ISO dates), good, and text.

Arguments: `by`, `good`, `limit`, `since`, `text`, `types`, `until`.

<!-- key: mcp:weak_springs -->
### weak_springs

A study's weak springs (ADR 0080): which bodies get them (held only by frictionless or frictional contact; with weak_springs 'always' also bodies held by nothing), the study's mode, factor and limit, and, for its latest stored run, the force they carried per step and any weak_springs_carry warning (the body never seated). Change the mode with an edit of the study's weak_springs (auto, always, never), weak_spring_factor or weak_spring_limit.

Arguments: `study`.

<!-- key: mcp:weld_add -->
### weld_add

Plan a weld between two parts (ADR 0078): `part` and the `edges` it runs along, by name (an edge is named by its two faces, 'B/-x|B/-z'; selections_check lists them). Of each edge's faces the one lying on another part is the seat; the other carries the first leg, and the other part's touching face the second. `leg` a quantity (a fillet's leg, a groove's depth), `leg2` an unequal fillet's other leg; `type` fillet or groove (`groove` cjp or pjp); `pattern` continuous or intermittent (`segment`, `pitch`). A light weld (springs across the joint, line force at stations; CalculiX for now). Returns `batch` to pass to submit (one undo).

Arguments: `component`, `edges`, `groove`, `leg`, `leg2`, `name`, `part`, `pattern`, `pitch`, `segment`, `type`.

<!-- key: mcp:weld_fatigue -->
### weld_fatigue

A light weld's fatigue by AISC 360-16 Appendix 3 (ADR 0078 step 5; AWS D1.1's nontubular categories are the same): the stress range between `steps` (two 1-based steps with weld results, or one: from zero; default the last from zero) against F_SR for `cycles` and the detail's `category` (Table A-3.1): 'F' (default) shear on the fillet's throat from the line forces; A, B, B', C, D, E, E' the base metal at the weld's toe (the largest principal stress range at its footprint nodes, mesh-dependent). Returns the range, F_SR, the ratio (≤ 1 passes) and where. `method='asme'`: ASME VIII-2 5.5.5's equivalent structural stress at the attachment's toe (the path's part) from the weld's line forces and moments, membrane f/t plus bending 6m/t², t `thickness_m` (a shell's own by default); returns each station's permissible cycles on Table 3-F.2M's `basis` curve (default -3sigma; `material` steel or aluminium) and, with `cycles`, the damage. `side='plate'`: the toe on the other part (a light weld on solids), from the plate's own section through its thickness there, its thickness measured unless given.

Arguments: `basis`, `category`, `cycles`, `material`, `method`, `side`, `steps`, `study`, `thickness_m`, `weld`.

<!-- key: mcp:weld_make_line -->
### weld_make_line

Turn a modelled weld (ADR 0078 step 4) back into a light weld: its bead's part, geometry, material, ties and mesh size removed. Returns `batch` to pass to submit (one undo); nothing is made here.

Arguments: `component`, `weld`.

<!-- key: mcp:weld_make_modelled -->
### weld_make_modelled

Draw a light weld as a modelled bead (ADR 0078 step 4): a fillet (straight, a polyline, a curve, all round, or intermittent: a bead per segment) becomes a part of its own (`weld_bead` steps: its legs from the weld's node pairs on the component's mesh, its root cut back a tenth of the leg so the plates meet only through it), its filler (or the path's part's material) as its material, its legs tied to the two faces, elements a sixth of the leg in it. Its line forces then come from the section through its throat (weld_results, the same checks; the section's force is mesh-dependent through the root's notch, about 1 % at six elements). Meshes the component to find the legs. A groove weld gets no bead: its faces are tied over its depth at the solve, and with `reinforcement` set its cap is drawn as a part `<weld> cap` tied to the plates (`cap_faces`, found from the face selections at the path if unset). Returns `batch` to pass to submit (one undo); nothing is made here.

Arguments: `component`, `weld`.

<!-- key: mcp:weld_results -->
### weld_results

Light welds' results in a study's latest run (ADR 0078): per weld its total force (N), largest line force (N/m) and where, mean line force, welded length, and each station's line force in the weld's frame (along, throat_normal, throat_shear, magnitude, x, y, z; twist N·m/m about the path), and `strength`: AISC 360-16 J2 at the governing station (filler and F_EXX, throat, design and allowable strength per length, LRFD and ASD utilisations for loads factored that way; `directional` takes Eq. J2-5's 1 + 0.5 sin^1.5 θ, allowed for linear welds loaded in plane) and `instantaneous_centre`: the group's in-plane force and moment about its centroid against its strength by the instantaneous centre of rotation (AISC 360-10 J2.4(b), the Manual's Part 8 method; P_n, eccentricity, LRFD and ASD utilisations; out-of-plane bending noted, not covered). `weld` one of them; `step` 1-based among the steps with weld results (default the last).

Arguments: `directional`, `step`, `study`, `weld`.
